one_line: Adaptive cooking practice workspace shared by learner and agent.
what_it_does: Guides beginners through progressive recipe and technique practice with preferences, one-step mode, persistence, and human-approved progress.
leverage_rationale: Shared structured recipe/session state, constraint-aware composition, and approval-gated completion make the agent materially more reliable than UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text describes eleven page tools sharing the visible cooking workspace.
Context tokens and revision checks address stale recipe changes; completion and memory require human approval.
execution_rationale: The packet gives unusually detailed workflow, validation, and regression evidence, with the frame sheet showing the branded recipe UI; end-to-end video evidence is absent.
execution_evidence: Claims 36 automated tests plus lint, typecheck, build, browser checks, and fixes for paused-session and servings-change bugs.
Frame sheet shows coherent Mise recipe-entry and recipe-line presentation.
impact_rationale: Clear beginner-cooking audience and a credible progression-based intervention for making cooking manageable.
impact_evidence: Pitch explicitly targets learning one dish and technique at a time.
Four recipe lines and forty levels are described.
creativity_rationale: A thoughtful synthesis of adaptive cooking pedagogy, shared state, and human-controlled agent assistance.
creativity_evidence: Completion cannot be awarded by an agent and suggested memory remains pending until approval.
Technique progression is integrated into recipe adaptation.
usability_note: Visible entry flow and recipe cards appear approachable; accessibility and mobile checks are claimed.
red_flags: No submitted video despite frame-sheet paths; recipes are not professionally cook-tested or allergy-certified.
standouts: Strong safety and shared-state framing for a beginner-learning workflow.
Explicit regression fixes and boundary disclosures.
advance_reason: Strong evidence-backed product concept with meaningful WebMCP collaboration value.

one_line: A lab that compares human and agent task journeys and repairs parity gaps.
what_it_does: Runs paired traces through a deterministic event-registration scenario, scores parity across outcome, information, consent, state, and effort, then applies a human-approved contract patch.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is one half of the experimental instrument and exposes structured, stateful traces that UI automation cannot reliably reproduce for parity testing.
leverage_evidence: Ten page-side tools share state with the visible interface.
Baseline parity 50/100 rises to 96/100 after a guarded completion contract and clearer wording.
execution_rationale: The scenario, intentional defects, repair, and quantitative retest form a coherent product loop, though no actual video frames are available beyond packaging preview.
execution_evidence: Packet specifies three intentional problems and a four-part patch.
Devpost screenshot preview visibly presents the demo as a human/agent journey comparison.
impact_rationale: Provides a concrete method for teams to detect dangerous divergence between human UX and agent UX.
impact_evidence: Measures missing fees, policy information, consent gates, final state, and effort.
Produces evidence-backed findings and retest score.
creativity_rationale: The dual usability laboratory and parity metric are a memorable, original interaction model for WebMCP quality assurance.
creativity_evidence: Human and agent traces are deliberately paired and repaired together.
Human approval of the patch is intentionally not agent-callable.
usability_note: The lab framing and deterministic scenario appear clear and inspectable.
red_flags: Quantitative parity claims are primarily self-reported in the packet; no playable observation here.
standouts: Explicitly tests WebMCP's human-agent parity rather than merely adding tools.
Strong safety and consent findings.
advance_reason: Distinctive, directly relevant WebMCP evaluation product with a credible measured repair loop.

one_line: A consent and audit hook for risky WebMCP tool calls.
what_it_does: Adds risk metadata, selective approval cards, audit logging, attention cues, and optional WebAuthn to WebMCP tool registration.
leverage_rationale: Consent, typed risk semantics, and audit state change the safety properties of agent calls beyond what generic UI automation provides.
leverage_evidence: Packet distinguishes auto-approved reads from approval-gated high-risk actions.
Visible demo preview shows Monitoring, Service Health, tool risk, and Audit Log surfaces.
execution_rationale: The package-plus-demo scope is coherent and the packaging preview shows an intentional monitoring UI, but no actual frame/video proof of invocation is supplied.
execution_evidence: Claims a reusable hook/provider and consuming demo app.
Screenshot visibly identifies a healthy service-health panel and empty audit log.
impact_rationale: Addresses a real safety gap for sites exposing agents to consequential actions, with reusable infrastructure value.
impact_evidence: Examples include rollback and deployment operations.
Audit records approved, denied, and auto-approved calls.
creativity_rationale: A strong and timely safety synthesis with selective consent and cross-tab cues, though the package pattern is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Optional biometric gate for irreversible actions.
Favicon/title attention cues for pending approvals.
usability_note: Selective interruption and explicit stakes should reduce approval fatigue.
red_flags: No submitted video; biometric and runtime compatibility claims are not independently demonstrated in the packet.
standouts: Consent is structural and reusable rather than a prompt convention.
Auditability is treated as a first-class product surface.
advance_reason: Important reusable infrastructure with clear safety value and coherent demo evidence.

one_line: Collaborative survey quality and safety review with structured agent tools.
what_it_does: Detects privacy, bias, wording, and response-design issues, explains findings, proposes corrections, and recomputes readiness before publication.
leverage_rationale: Structured inspect/validate/explain/correct/verify operations on shared survey state are materially more precise and repeatable than scraping a form.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes human-agent shared state and structured correction/verification tools.
Visible preview headline says agents can fix bad surveys and shows a validation-oriented presentation.
execution_rationale: The described review-correction-verification loop is coherent, but evidence is mostly text and a Devpost media preview rather than observed product execution.
execution_evidence: Specific example detects unnecessary personal-information request as blocking and recommends safer wording.
Claims readiness score updates after correction.
impact_rationale: Survey researchers and product teams have a real recurring quality, privacy, and bias problem that this workflow directly addresses.
impact_evidence: Lists leading language, double-barrelled questions, unclear timeframes, sensitive questions, and conflicting options.
Correction and readiness verification are part of the stated workflow.
creativity_rationale: A useful human-agent review synthesis with meaningful safety emphasis, though the category is established.
creativity_evidence: Combines explainable findings, blocking severity, correction, and post-fix verification.
Keeps people in control while agents inspect and repair.
usability_note: The review findings/readiness framing appears understandable; detailed interaction evidence is limited.
red_flags: No public repository and no submitted frame sheets; claims are not deeply observable from the packet.
standouts: Concrete privacy issue and blocking remediation example.
Clear before-publication audience and workflow.
advance_reason: Credible audience/problem fit and meaningful structured review workflow, despite thin execution evidence.

one_line: A round-based strategy/action game playable against humans or agents.
what_it_does: Combines Worms-like skill action with Civilization-like strategy and lets users play an agent via an invite link.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP removes setup friction and enables an agent opponent in a real-time round-based game where ordinary UI driving would be slow and token-heavy.
leverage_evidence: Packet says MCP protocol was optimized for fast agent reactions within round limits.
WebMCP lets a user paste an invite link and play without complicated MCP setup.
execution_rationale: A playable match is claimed and the screenshot packaging is coherent, but no frame sheets were submitted and end-to-end operation is not evidenced.
execution_evidence: About text reports playing matches against an agent and a BabylonJS/TypeScript implementation.
Devpost screenshot shows a game demo preview/lobby presentation.
impact_rationale: A clear entertainment and novelty audience exists for accessible human-agent competitive play.
impact_evidence: Pitch explicitly supports agent-vs-agent and agent-vs-human matches.
Invite-link model lowers participation friction.
creativity_rationale: The Worms/Civilization hybrid plus agent-versus-agent play is an ambitious and memorable game interaction.
creativity_evidence: Combines round strategy with skill-based action.
Author reports reflecting on agent/game-AI behavior through matches.
usability_note: Invite-link access is promising, but game usability and responsiveness are not demonstrated in submitted frames.
red_flags: No frame sheets; repository is not public; claims rely heavily on self-report.
standouts: Agent play is central rather than decorative.
Protocol latency constraints are directly addressed.
advance_reason: Original agent-game concept with meaningful WebMCP necessity, but execution evidence is thin.

one_line: A contract review workspace where agents propose but cannot apply redlines.
what_it_does: Reads clauses, flags risks, compares terms to a playbook, drafts replacement language, and routes every change through human accept/reject controls.
leverage_rationale: Clause-anchored live document state, typed IDs, and structural prohibition of agent mutation create safety and repeatability unavailable to a chat upload or generic UI agent.
leverage_evidence: No mutation tool is registered and the server refuses writes tagged as agent.
Suggestions are clause objects with status, reasoning, and human acceptance; live state avoids stale uploads.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a highly coherent scoped workflow and multiple explicit safety invariants; visual/video execution remains only partial.
execution_evidence: Describes clause-by-clause review through accept/reject redlines.
Devpost has extensive packaging and gallery evidence, though no submitted video frames verified here.
impact_rationale: Contract signers and teams face a concrete high-stakes comprehension problem, and the product directly reduces risk while preserving human authority.
impact_evidence: Flags financial consequences with severity and plain-English explanations.
Human acceptance is the only contract-mutating action.
creativity_rationale: The by-construction no-write agent architecture is a strong interaction and safety concept beyond generic contract summarization.
creativity_evidence: Safety boundary is enforced by capability absence, not behavioral instruction.
Redline objects are anchored to document clauses.
usability_note: Redline review and accept/reject affordances map to familiar document workflows.
red_flags: No public repository and no submitted frame sheets; legal-quality claims should not be inferred.
standouts: Excellent structural safety boundary.
Strong live-state rationale for WebMCP over chat uploads.
advance_reason: One of the clearest high-stakes WebMCP use cases, with unusually strong safety-by-construction reasoning.

one_line: A cozy farm simulator where humans and agents share daily work.
what_it_does: Lets players farm, buy equipment, trade goods, manage stamina/time, and delegate work to an agent through an integrated WebMCP inspector.
leverage_rationale: Shared game state and task delegation make agent participation useful, but much of the game outcome could plausibly be driven through UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Packet emphasizes divvying up daily farm work and a detailed in-game WebMCP inspector.
Tools expose game actions and shared state, but indispensability is less clear than in safety/state-heavy products.
execution_rationale: The scope is coherent and the gallery/frame references support a complete cozy-game presentation, though no video transcript or direct observed run is available.
execution_evidence: Describes farming progression, market, rest/day cycle, and collaboration loop.
Claims a detailed inspector built into the game.
impact_rationale: Credible entertainment value and a thoughtful exploratory audience interested in everyday human-agent collaboration.
impact_evidence: Inspiration directly explores delegating routine work so people can focus on enjoyable activities.
Game provides a legible sandbox for agent collaboration.
creativity_rationale: The cozy-farming metaphor is familiar, but the agent labor-sharing framing and transparent inspector add a fresh angle.
creativity_evidence: Human and agent are intentionally placed on similar footing.
Under-the-hood tool inspector is integrated into the game.
usability_note: Familiar farming loops likely aid onboarding; agent collaboration details are not fully observable.
red_flags: Agent value may be convenience rather than transformative; no direct agent invocation evidence.
standouts: Strong thematic framing of human/agent division of labor.
Transparent inspector supports learnability and trust.
advance_reason: Complete-feeling game concept with clear human-agent collaboration and good category fit.

one_line: An explorable pixel-art portfolio shared by visitors and page-aware agents.
what_it_does: Provides an HD-2D world, landmark navigation, personalized tours, page-specific inspection, biography/research tools, and explicit human-controlled copying.
leverage_rationale: Page-aware tools and shared route state improve agent navigation and context, though a general agent could reproduce much of the browsing outcome with friction.
leverage_evidence: Global and page-specific tools move with the visible route and expose the same interface state.
Agent can create goal-specific tours and walk the on-screen traveler to landmarks.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent portfolio world and rights-safe competition edition with multiple interaction modes; frame sheets are available but end-to-end video proof is absent.
execution_evidence: Keyboard, mouse, touch, and agent navigation are all described.
Sanitized Mods page and explicit human-only copying show deliberate packaging and boundaries.
impact_rationale: Recruiters, collaborators, technical reviewers, and creative visitors have a credible need for tailored portfolio exploration.
impact_evidence: Goal-specific tours address differing visitor information needs.
Research tools provide publication metadata and paste-ready BibTeX.
creativity_rationale: A memorable playable portfolio/world as an agent-human shared interface is highly original and pursued deeply.
creativity_evidence: Visitors and agents inhabit the same navigable pixel world.
Page-aware tool registration changes with route and content context.
usability_note: Multiple input modes and landmarks support exploration, but a game-like portfolio may add discovery friction.
red_flags: The packet says it began as a personal hub world, so the competition extension is meaningful but not wholly new.
standouts: Unusually memorable portfolio interaction model.
Rights-safe sanitization and human-controlled copying are thoughtful.
advance_reason: Highly creative, coherent shared-world portfolio with credible agent-aware navigation.

one_line: A bounded educational app for classifying whether evidence supports a claim.
what_it_does: Takes a claim and evidence, returns SUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED, or INSUFFICIENT with bounded probabilities through the same human and WebMCP analysis path.
leverage_rationale: The typed tool shares the bounded analysis path and fails closed on missing evidence, improving consistency, but the core task is also simple through a UI.
leverage_evidence: Same analyze(claim,evidence) function powers human interface and WebMCP tool.
Browser canary discovered and invoked the tool; blank evidence blocks rather than producing a verdict.
execution_rationale: The scope is intentionally small and safety-bounded, with regression and browser-canary claims, but no frame sheets and demo status unknown.
execution_evidence: Claims automated model/UI regression tests and a headed-Chrome WebMCP canary.
Explicit claim ceiling and BLOCK state define coherent boundaries.
impact_rationale: Students have a real need for a transparent method to compare claims and evidence without overclaiming truth detection.
impact_evidence: Educational evidence-assessment framing is explicit.
Outputs bounded classifications rather than a general fact-check verdict.
creativity_rationale: A sound educational application with disciplined safety boundaries, but the concept and interaction are relatively familiar.
creativity_evidence: Explicitly limits scope to educational evidence assessment.
Human and agent paths share identical bounded logic.
usability_note: Two-input classification is likely approachable; observed UI evidence is absent.
red_flags: No frame sheets; demo_alive is unknown; execution claims are not visually checkable.
standouts: Excellent claim ceiling and fail-closed behavior.
Clear educational audience and bounded output semantics.
advance_reason: Strong educational fit and responsible bounded design, with modest novelty and thin visual evidence.

one_line: A shared, provenance-aware canvas for safe low-voltage electronics troubleshooting.
what_it_does: Captures human symptoms and measurements, maps topology, ranks hypotheses, maintains a safe test plan, records history, and drafts a diagnostic report.
leverage_rationale: Typed tools over live topology, stable IDs, provenance, unit/power validation, reviewable writes, and undo provide structured collaboration that scraping cannot comparably guarantee.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes twelve tools sharing the same live case state.
Every write is visible, attributed, reviewable, and reversible; agent cannot pretend it observed hardware.
execution_rationale: The product architecture and safety workflow are unusually coherent, but no frame sheets or video are submitted and completion is primarily claimed.
execution_evidence: Describes case/canvas, hypothesis updates, safe test plan, append-only history, and report generation.
Strict schemas, revision checks, and undo are specified.
impact_rationale: Hobbyists and technicians face a real organization and safety problem when troubleshooting physical electronics with an agent.
impact_evidence: Human supplies de-energized measurements while agent organizes context and hypotheses.
Safety boundary prevents invented hardware observations and unsafe action authority.
creativity_rationale: The explicit human-sensor/agent-structure division and provenance-first diagnostic canvas are an ambitious, original application of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Agent records only values explicitly supplied by the human.
Shared command layer makes validation, history, proposals, and undo identical across actors.
usability_note: A structured canvas and report could reduce troubleshooting cognitive load; visual usability is unverified.
red_flags: No submitted frame sheets or video; demo evidence is limited to the written packet.
Safety usefulness depends on careful real-world interpretation beyond the app.
standouts: Strong provenance and anti-hallucination boundary for physical-world assistance.
Undo/reviewability treats agent writes as accountable state changes.
advance_reason: High WebMCP leverage and meaningful safety-oriented niche impact despite thin execution evidence.
